OVERVIEW. The page has two parts. The upper third derives the functional equation of Dirichlet L-series modulo a prime q, using Riemann's 1859 contour-integral method and Gauss sums. The lower two thirds concern the prime-power sum psi(x)=sum_{p^k<=x} log p. There Riemann (i) derives what is now the von Mangoldt explicit formula from his own formula for f(x); (ii) integrates it; (iii) checks its constant -log 2pi independently via int psi d(x^-2) = zeta'(2)/zeta(2) and the sum over zeros; (iv) recomputes Sum_{alpha>0} 1/(alpha^2+1/4) numerically to 20 places; (v) starts a Laplace-transform explicit formula for Sum Lambda(n) e^{-ny}. Notation: Pi(s)=Gamma(s+1). psi(s)=dlog Pi(s)/ds, i.e. digamma(s+1), so psi(0)=-C. Zeros are written rho=1/2+alpha i.

A. DIRICHLET L-SERIES MOD q.
(1) Let q be prime, g a primitive root, Ind n the index of n to base g, and alpha a (q-1)-th root of unity. Then chi(n)=alpha^{Ind n} is a Dirichlet character. Write chi(s)=prod_p 1/(1-p^{-s} alpha^{Ind p})=sum_n alpha^{Ind n} n^{-s}, i.e. modern L(s,chi).
(2) Pi(s-1) n^{-s}=int_0^oo e^{-nx} x^{s-1} dx. Summing over n in residue classes gives Gamma(s)L(s,chi)=sum_{n=1}^{q-1} alpha^{Ind n} int_0^oo e^{-nx} x^{s-1}/(1-e^{-qx}) dx. The image/transcription reads 1-e^{qx}; the sign of the exponent must be negative.
(3) Substitute x -> x/q and replace the real ray by a loop around the positive axis; this is exactly the 1859 zeta argument. This produces the factor (e^{pi i s}-e^{-pi i s}), written sin(pi s) up to the factor 2i, and q^s.
(4) The integrand e^{-nx/q}/(1-e^{-x}) has poles at x=2 pi i m. Their residues give i sum_m sum_n rho^{-nm} alpha^{Ind n} (2 pi i m)^{s-1}(-2 pi i), with rho=e^{2 pi i/q}.
(5) Substituting n -> n m^{-1} gives sum_n rho^{-nm} alpha^{Ind n}=alpha^{-Ind m} sum_n rho^{-n} alpha^{Ind n}. The double sum therefore factors as a Gauss sum times sum_m alpha^{-Ind m} m^{s-1}, i.e. L(1-s, chi-bar). Result: Gamma(s) L(s,chi) q^s (trig factor) = Gauss sum x (2pi)^s x L(1-s, chi-bar). This is the functional equation linking L(s,chi) and L(1-s,chi-bar).
(6) Gauss-sum modulus. Let tau=sum_{n=1}^{q-1} rho^n alpha^{Ind n}. Then
 tau * sum_{n'} rho^{n'} alpha^{-Ind n'} = sum_{sigma} alpha^{Ind sigma} sum_{n'} rho^{(sigma+1)n'}   (put n = sigma n').
 The inner sum is q-1 if sigma = -1 and -1 otherwise. Hence the total is -sum_sigma alpha^{Ind sigma} + q alpha^{Ind(-1)} = q alpha^{(q-1)/2}, since Ind(-1)=(q-1)/2 and alpha is nontrivial. Riemann notes alpha^{Ind(-1)} = +-1 (even or odd character). From this he gets (tau/sqrt q)(conj tau/sqrt q)=1, i.e. |tau|=sqrt q.
(7) Completed function: xi_q(t) = Pi(s/2-1) q^{s/2} sqrt(sum q^{-1/2} rho^n alpha^{-Ind n}) pi^{-s/2} L(s,chi). This is Gamma(s/2)(q/pi)^{s/2} L(s,chi), times the square root of the normalized Gauss sum (the modern root number). It is the even-character analogue of xi(t), normalized so that the functional equation becomes symmetric.
(8) log L(s,chi)=sum p^{-s} alpha^{Ind p}+1/2 sum p^{-2s} alpha^{Ind p^2}+... and L'/L=-sum log p * p^{-s} alpha^{Ind p}/(1-p^{-s} alpha^{Ind p}). The denominator as transcribed is garbled. Then log L(s,chi)/s = int_1^oo f_chi(x) x^{-s-1} dx, the L-analogue of Riemann's log zeta(s)/s=int f(x)x^{-s-1}dx, written using s int_{p^k}^oo x^{-s-1}dx = p^{-ks}.

B. EXPLICIT FORMULA FOR psi(x).
(1) Chebyshev functions: theta(x)=sum_{p<x} log p (written 'Prod log p', meaning log prod p); psi(x)=theta(x)+theta(x^{1/2})+...; log prod_{n<x} n = psi(x)+psi(x/2)+....
(2) log p=int_1^p dy/y. Hence int_1^x (F(x)-F(y))dy/y = int_1^x log y dF(y). With F=pi this gives theta; with F = Riemann's f = sum pi(x^{1/n})/n it gives psi(x)=int_1^x (f(x)-f(y))dy/y = int_1^x log y df(y).
(3) Insert Riemann's 1859 formula f(x)=Li(x)-sum[Li(x^{1/2+alpha i})+Li(x^{1/2-alpha i})]+int_x^oo dt/(t(t^2-1)log t)+log xi(0). Since log y dLi(y^rho)=y^{rho-1}dy, each zero contributes (x^rho-1)/rho (the struck line). The last term gives int dx/(x(x^2-1)), computed in the margin as log x-1/2 log(x^2-1), i.e. -1/2 log(1-x^-2).
(4) Result: psi(x)=x-sum_{alpha>0}[x^{1/2+alpha i}/(1/2+alpha i)+x^{1/2-alpha i}/(1/2-alpha i)]-1/2 log(1-1/x^2)-log 2pi.
 In real form: x - x^{1/2} sum (cos(alpha log x)+2 alpha sin(alpha log x))/(alpha^2+1/4) - ....
(5) Integrating term by term: int_1^x psi = x^2/2 - sum[x^{3/2+alpha i}/((1/2+alpha i)(3/2+alpha i))+c.c.] - 1/2 x log(1-1/x^2) + 1/2 log((x-1)/(x+1)) - x log 2pi + const.
 At x=1 the two log terms combine to -log 2, giving 0 = 1/2 - Sigma(...) - log 2 - log 2pi + Const.

C. CHECK OF THE CONSTANT -log 2pi.
(1) int_1^oo psi(x) d(x^-2) = -sum_{p^k} log p * p^{-2k} = zeta'(2)/zeta(2) = -sum(log n/n^2)/sum(1/n^2).
(2) Computed termwise from the explicit formula, with integrand psi*(-2x^-3) = -2x^-2 + 2 sum x^{-5/2+alpha i}/(1/2+alpha i) + x^-3 log(1-x^-2) + (constant) x^-3:
 - the x term gives -2;
 - the zeros give sum over rho of [1/(2-rho)+1/rho], written via 1/(-3/2+alpha i) and 1/(1/2+alpha i);
 - the log term gives -1/2. He proves this with the antiderivative 1/2(1-x^-2)log(1-x^-2)+1/2 x^-2.
 - the constant K gives +-K.
(3) Evaluate the zero sums from the product for xi:
 - sum 1/(2-rho) = xi'/xi(2) = 1/2 psi(1) + 1 - 1/2 log pi + zeta'(2)/zeta(2);
 - sum 1/rho = 1 - 1/2 log pi - 1/2 psi(0) - log 2.
(4) Everything cancels to -log pi - log 2 - K = 0. This confirms that the constant has magnitude log 2pi (= zeta'(0)/zeta(0)).
(5) Auxiliary steps:
 - Euler-Maclaurin: zeta(s)=sum_1^m n^-s + m^{1-s}/(s-1) - 1/2 m^-s, hence dlog[(s-1)zeta]/ds at s=1 equals sum 1/n - log m -> -psi(0)=C;
 - recursions psi(n)=1/n+psi(n-1), psi(0)=-1+psi(1);
 - limit formulas for psi(0), 1/2 psi(0), 1/2 psi(1/2), giving psi(0)-1/2 psi(1/2) = 1/2 psi(0) + log 2 - 1.

D. NUMERICS. From 1/2 log pi + psi(0) - 1/2 psi(1/2) + sum 1/(alpha^2+1/4) = 0:
 log pi = 1.14472 98858 49400 17415, log 4 = 1.38629 43611 19890 61883;
 sum = 2.53102 42469 69290 79298; minus C = 0.57721 56649 01532 86061 gives 1.95380 85820 67757 93237;
 half = 0.97690 42910 33878 96618; so sum_{alpha>0} 1/(alpha^2+1/4) = 0.02309 57089 66121 03381.

E. LAPLACE TRANSFORM (start). Using y int_0^oo e^{-yx} x^rho/rho dx = Gamma(rho) y^{-rho}:
 y int_1^oo e^{-yx} psi(x) dx = Pi(0)/y - sum[Pi(-1/2+alpha i) y^{-1/2-alpha i} + c.c.] + ....
 The left side equals sum Lambda(n) e^{-ny}. The binomial expansion Pi(a-1)(1-e^{-y})^{-a} = sum Pi(a-1+k) e^{-ky}/k! appears, as does a Mellin-Barnes integral int Pi(n+s) d log zeta. This leads into the next page's series sum log n * e^{-n^2 x}.
errors: In chi(s)Pi(s-1) the denominator must be 1-e^{-qx}; 1-e^{qx} as transcribed is a slip (or a misreading).
The contour step: the factor should be (e^{pi i s}-e^{-pi i s}) = 2i sin(pi s); 'sin pi s' alone drops a constant. This is bookkeeping only.
The Gauss-sum result q*alpha^{(q-1)/2} is correct only for a nontrivial character, where sum alpha^{Ind sigma}=0; this is implicitly assumed.
The L'/L formula as transcribed has denominator 1-p^{(q-1)s}; correct is 1-p^{-s}alpha^{Ind p}.
'Prod_{p<x} log p = theta(x)' should read sum (or log prod p).
Real form of the explicit formula: x^rho/rho + c.c. = x^{1/2}(cos(alpha log x)+2 alpha sin(alpha log x))/(alpha^2+1/4). An extra factor 2 in front of the sum, if present, is wrong.

The sign convention of K is inconsistent: with integrand term +2K/x^3 the final relation should give K = +log 2pi (psi = ... - K). The page's '-log pi - log 2 - K = 0' corresponds to psi = ... + K. The magnitude log 2pi is right either way.

In the termwise integral the bracket written 2Sigma[1/((-3/2+alpha i)(1/2+alpha i))] needs a minus sign. The subsequent partial-fraction form -Sigma 1/(-3/2+alpha i) + Sigma 1/(1/2+alpha i) is correct.
The binomial expansion is written with (e^{-y}-1) instead of (1-e^{-y}), and the k! denominators appear only from the third term.
The limit formulas for psi(0), 1/2 psi(1/2) are stated without lim and with the summation index reused as the bound. They are correct as limits.
Last digit of 0.02309570896612103381: the true value is ...03382 (rounding).
